etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Latin lēns (“lentil”), with Medieval Latin later taking on the sense of “lens”, a semantic loan from Arabic عَدْسَة (ʕadsa, “lentil; optic lens”).

definitions.definition: (optics) An object, usually made of glass, that focuses or defocuses the light that passes through it.

quote.citation: 2013 July-August, Catherine Clabby, “Focus on Everything”, in American Scientist:
quote.text: Not long ago, it was difficult to produce photographs of tiny creatures with every part in focus. That’s because the lenses that are excellent at magnifying tiny subjects produce a narrow depth of field.

definitions.definition: A device which focuses or defocuses electron beams.
(geometry) A convex shape bounded by two circular arcs, joined at their endpoints, the corresponding concave shape being a lune.
(biology) A genus of the legume family; its bean.
(anatomy) The transparent crystalline structure in the eye.

quote.citation: 2013 July-August, Fenella Saunders, “Tiny Lenses See the Big Picture”, in American Scientist:
quote.text: The single-imaging optic of the mammalian eye offers some distinct visual advantages. Such lenses can take in photons from a wide range of angles, increasing light sensitivity. They also have high spatial resolution, resolving incoming images in minute detail.

definitions.definition: (earth science) A body of rock, ice, or water shaped like a convex lens.
(programming) A construct used in statically-typed functional programming languages to access nested data structures.
(by extension, figuratively) A way of looking, literally or figuratively, at something.

quote.citation: 2004 April 11, Ann Hulbert, “Are the Kids All Right?”, in The New York Times Magazine, page 11:
quote.text: If "the public looks at the condition of America's children largely through a negative lens," worries Child Trends […] , "it may be more difficult to  […]  promote child well-being."

quote.citation: 2023 April 26, Benjamin Lee, quoting Steven Spielberg, “Steven Spielberg: ‘No film should be revised’ based on modern sensitivity”, in The Guardian‎[1], →ISSN:
quote.text: No film should be revised based on the lenses we now are, either voluntarily, or being forced to peer through.

quote.citation: 2020 May 7, Katie Rife, “If you’re looking to jump in your seat, make a playdate with Z”, in The Onion AV Club‎[2], archived from the original on 16 May 2020:
quote.text: It’s set in an anonymous, upper-middle-class suburb, lensed in the generic gunmetal gray that will one day appear as dated as the fuzzy outlines of ’80s direct-to-video horror movies.

definitions.definition: (geology) To become thinner towards the edges.
